written_before: the first archive slot job and the first K3 anchor call; after 136 fast calls (K2 of the 8 gated cases, their location phases and priority-2 1k grids; 0 failures, 0 differences) and one single archive call (mobilenet_v2-int6 sat.w20 0-128, launched 17:23:54 by the runner of addendum 3)

deviations.what: archive runs inside slot jobs (mechanics only)
deviations.rule: The archive's runs (the two ungated cases, addendum-2 tiles unchanged) and the K3 anchor calls are made like the fast runs: one GPU job (tools/run/accumulator_sweep_mn_fastjob.py --engine archive inside gpu_run.sh --min-free-mib 3000) runs successive archive calls ($M/run.sh predict ... --batch 8, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, one process per call) for at most 720 s of new calls, rebuilding the queue after each call. Reason: the fast cases' location and priority-2 grids finished in 15 minutes, while each single archive call waits about 10 minutes for a GPU slot; the two ungated cases' remaining ~60 calls would otherwise take most of a day. Which runs are made is unchanged.

deviations.what: budget accounting of archive calls inside slot jobs
deviations.rule: Counted by the job's wall time (logs/fast-jobs.jsonl, engine 'archive'), as fast jobs are; their per-call logs go to logs/jobarchive/<case>/ (not logs/<case>/), so the first runner's ledger rule does not count them a second time. Single archive calls of earlier runners keep the addendum-1/2 rule.

At most 2 GPU jobs of the lane at a time (unchanged); the runner starts at most one new slot job per engine per pass, a second one of the same engine only when at least 6 runs of that engine are queued.
Slot-job logs are logs/run2-fastjobs/<time>-<engine>-<n>.log (addendum 3's runner wrote two jobs started in the same second into one file: cosmetic, both calls lists are complete).
